gaps.sentence: I am afraid you ___ park here without a resident's permit.
gaps.hint: permission that is refused with cannot

gaps.sentence: You ___ have worried — everything turned out fine.
gaps.hint: the worry was unnecessary in the end
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have' means the action happened but was unnecessary: needn't have.

gaps.sentence: You ___ told me — I would have kept the evening free!
gaps.explanation: 'Should have' plus the participle criticizes something that did not happen: should have told.

gaps.sentence: You have been travelling all day, so you ___ be exhausted.
gaps.hint: an obvious conclusion from known facts
gaps.explanation: A logical conclusion from known facts uses 'must': must be exhausted.

gaps.sentence: I do not know whose coat this is — it ___ belong to one of the guests.
gaps.explanation: 'Might' hedges a guess when the speaker is not sure: might belong.

gaps.sentence: She ___ to pass one more exam to qualify as an architect.
gaps.explanation: 'Need to' conjugates like a normal verb: she needs to pass.

gaps.sentence: When I was a child, I ___ stay up late on New Year's Eve.
gaps.hint: permission that existed in the past
gaps.explanation: 'Was allowed to' expresses past permission; 'could' is also possible: was allowed to.

gaps.sentence: You ___ pay for children under six — entry is free for them.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' expresses absence of necessity: needn't pay.
